title: How to Keep People and Distractions Out of Product Photos
description: Learn when background removal, cropping, reshooting, or a licensed object-removal editor is the right way to handle people and distractions.

blocks.text: You finally got the perfect product photo. Great lighting. Nice angle. Product looks premium. But there's a random person in the background. Or your hand is visible. Or a customer walked into frame.
Here's how to fix it in under a minute.
Why This Matters More Than You Think
Random people in product photos:

items.text: Trigger buyer distraction
Look unprofessional
Sometimes violate marketplace rules (Amazon prohibits additional people in main images)
Break the "clean brand" aesthetic

blocks.text: Fixing them used to require Photoshop and 15+ minutes. Not anymore.
Choose the Right Cleanup Method

items.text: Upload your photo to edit-photo.com

The current edit-photo tool isolates a foreground subject; it is not a general object-removal or inpainting tool. For unwanted people or objects inside the scene, reshoot, crop, or use a licensed editor designed for that task.
If the person is inside the removable background, isolate the foreground product; otherwise crop, reshoot, or use a licensed inpainting editor.
Only a dedicated inpainting editor can reconstruct the scene, and the result still needs close visual review.
Download the clean photo

blocks.text: Works best when the person is against a relatively simple background (wall, sky, fabric). Complex backgrounds may need light touch-up.
Common Use Cases
Your hand or reflection. Shooting glossy products often catches your own reflection. Remove it.
Random shopper in background. Common in retail location shoots or lifestyle scenes.
Team member in the frame. Behind-the-scenes shots often have someone accidentally visible.
Old models you no longer want. Photos from a previous shoot with a model who's no longer with your brand.
When to Reshoot Instead
If the person occupies more than 30% of the frame, or is directly overlapping your product, edit tools struggle. In these cases:

items.text: Reshoot if easy
Or crop instead of removing
Or use a completely different angle

blocks.text: Beyond People: Objects You Can Remove
Different cleanup methods are suited to different problems:

items.text: Crop or reshoot when loose objects distract from the product.
Use a cleaner shooting location or a dedicated inpainting editor.
Clean the set before shooting whenever possible.
Adjust lighting or retouch shadows in a separate editor.
Control reflections during capture; background removal cannot erase reflections on the product.

blocks.text: The Lifestyle Shoot Rescue
Doing a lifestyle shoot in a public location? Random tourists, cars, and passersby ruin the frame. Shoot anyway, then clean up in post.
This saves you the cost of renting a private location for shoots. And edit-photo.com makes it fast enough to be practical.
The Bigger Workflow
Combine object removal with background removal:

items.text: Remove distracting people/objects
Then remove the entire background
Composite onto a clean setting

blocks.text: You essentially rescue any shoot no matter how chaotic the environment was.
Save Bad Shoots
Not every shoot day goes perfectly. Sometimes location, weather, or luck screws you. Rescue your shots free at edit-photo.com.
